title: Zig
subtitle: A small, explicit systems language: no hidden control flow, no hidden allocations, compile-time code instead of macros, and a toolchain that builds and cross-compiles C as well as Zig.
description: Zig is a general-purpose systems programming language created by Andrew Kelley and first announced in 2016. It aims at the territory of C: operating-system components, game engines, embedded firmware, databases, language runtimes and command-line tools. It keeps C's directness (you decide where every byte lives) while removing much of what makes C hard to get right: there is no preprocessor, no hidden control flow, no hidden memory allocation, and in its safe build modes the compiler inserts checks that turn overflow, out-of-bounds access and many other mistakes into clear crashes instead of silent corruption. Its signature idea is **comptime**: ordinary Zig code that runs at compile time, which replaces macros and templates. Zig also ships a complete C and C++ toolchain, so it is often used to build and cross-compile existing C projects.

**Zig has not reached version 1.0.** The language and especially its standard library change between releases, sometimes substantially, and code written for one version often needs updating for the next. This course is written for **Zig 0.17.1**, the current release as of late 2026, and every program in it was compiled and run with that version. If you use a newer version, expect some standard-library names to differ; the language reference and the standard library source that come with your compiler are the final word. The course assumes the Start level of [Lumenary CS](/en/cs/) or equivalent experience: you know what a variable, a loop and a function are. Knowing a little C helps in places but is not required.

To run the programs, download Zig from the [official download page](https://ziglang.org/download/), unpack it anywhere and put the directory on your `PATH`; the [getting-started guide](https://ziglang.org/learn/getting-started/) also lists package managers that carry it. Zig is a single download with no other dependencies. There is no official online playground; [Compiler Explorer](https://godbolt.org/) can compile Zig in the browser, though its versions may lag behind the latest release.

levels.title: The language
levels.summary: Zig's philosophy and toolchain, values, integer and float types, control flow, arrays, slices, pointers and strings, and structs, enums and tagged unions.

levels.title: Errors, memory and compile time
levels.summary: Error unions with try, catch and errdefer, optionals, explicit allocators and leak detection, and comptime: generic types and functions written in ordinary Zig.

levels.title: Tools, C and a complete program
levels.summary: Test blocks, the build system and packages, calling C and being called from it, and a complete expression calculator in idiomatic Zig.
